summary: std::bind generates a forwarding call wrapper for a callable. Calling this wrapper invokes the original callable with some arguments bound and others supplied at call time via placeholders (_1, _2, etc.).
cpp17_notes: C++17 deprecates result_type and argument_type aliases. C++20 makes bind constexpr. Modern C++ often prefers lambdas for simplicity, but bind remains useful for partial application and member function binding.
audio_thread_notes: std::bind MAY allocate memory internally. Avoid using bind on the audio thread. Prefer lambdas with capture-by-value for fixed parameters, or pre-bind during initialization and store the result for later invocation.
